title: French National Quantum Strategy Backs €14M ($16M USD) Qubit Control 2030 Consortium to Scale Cryogenic Photonic Interconnects - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
The French National Quantum Strategy has announced €14 million ($16 million) in France 2030 funding for Qubit Control 2030 (QC2030), a 48-month research and development consortium led by French deep-tech startup VIQTHOR to build an integrated, sovereign control and readout chain for solid-state quantum computers. Unveiled at the World Quantum Cannes Festival, labeled by Systematic Paris-Region, and operated through Bpifrance’s i-Démo program, the initiative unites five French enabling-technology companies to replace bulky copper coaxial wiring from room temperature down to 10 millikelvin for superconducting and spin qubit platforms.

Control electronics and coaxial cables currently account for more than 70% of total quantum computer hardware costs, or roughly €60,000 per qubit, creating severe thermal-load and spatial constraints inside dilution refrigerators. By combining photonic modulation, signal multiplexing, and superconducting flex interconnects, QC2030 aims to eliminate the wiring bottleneck that limits single-cryostat qubit counts while complementing France’s PROQCIMA quantum processor development program.

Running from October 2026 through September 2030, the consortium teams will co-locate on a shared cryogenic platform at the iXcampus technology hub in Saint-Germain-en-Laye to validate two single-cryostat demonstrators, scaling from 1,000 controlled qubits in 2028 to 10,000 qubits in 2030. French National Quantum Strategy coordinator Loïc Le Loarer noted that securing domestic supply across cryogenic interconnects, amplifiers, and photonic links is essential to industrializing fault-tolerant quantum computers.
